sources.title: Getting started | Solenta docs
sources.finding: Installed agent CLIs are discovered on PATH; adding a non-Git folder initializes Git.

sources.title: Threads and providers | Solenta docs
sources.locator: Threads and providers; Queue or steer
sources.finding: Threads retain provider sessions, models and permissions; Claude and Codex support live steering, while other providers queue follow-ups.

sources.title: Orchestration | Solenta docs
sources.finding: Local orchestrators fork worktree workers, communicate through MCP, collect results and integrate branches. Remote projects require plain threads by default.

sources.title: Guardrails and verification | Solenta docs
sources.finding: Verify command failure prevents green completion. Claude governance policies are limited to calls surfaced for approval.

sources.title: Other computers and SSH | Solenta docs
sources.finding: The app can install a Linux headless host over SSH; remote projects run CLIs there. Worktrees and orchestration remain local-only in v1.

sources.title: Phones and browsers | Solenta docs
sources.finding: Browser UI is served by the agent host with scoped device tokens, revocation and reconnect. Tailscale can provide HTTPS.

sources.title: Worktrees and pull requests | Solenta docs
sources.locator: Worktrees and pull requests; Development lanes
sources.finding: Per-thread worktrees, staged diffs, inline review prompts, PR actions, checkpoints, JSON export and optional independent-provider review are documented.

sources.title: External MCP pairing | Solenta docs
sources.finding: External MCP clients can launch and inspect tasks with scoped expiring revocable tokens; new work defaults to approval.

sources.title: Shared Memory for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor Agents
sources.finding: Project-scoped local SQLite memory carries provenance and citations, invalidates stale file references, and injects recalled context into provider requests.

sources.title: Inbox, Planboard, Review | Solenta docs
sources.finding: The Planboard is GitHub/GitLab issues, not a local tracker. Auto-dispatch skips blocked issues; review queues group PR attention.

sources.title: Spec mode | Solenta documentation
sources.finding: Thread artifacts progress through approved requirements, design and tasks. Dependency-aware dispatch and Converge operate on the task DAG.

sources.title: Skills | Solenta documentation
sources.finding: Users can import skills, MCP configurations and instructions; plugin/local command trust is separate.

sources.title: Automations | Solenta docs
sources.finding: Schedules and polled GitHub, Linear and Sentry events start threads; three consecutive failures pause an automation.

sources.title: Spend guardrails | Solenta docs
sources.finding: Daily and orchestration budgets gate new work; a configurable concurrency cap queues runs oldest first.

sources.title: Usage and fleet analytics | Solenta docs
sources.finding: Usage separates provider/model costs and provider quota windows; estimated model prices fill missing costs and fleet metrics use Git/GitHub.

sources.title: Review itinerary | Solenta docs
sources.finding: Working-tree changes receive a risk-ranked review order that places CI/config changes first.

sources.title: Architecture | Solenta docs
sources.finding: Electron main manages processes, local storage and scheduling; the UI is React over typed IPC.

sources.title: Solenta: run Claude Code, Codex and Cursor in parallel
sources.finding: macOS Apple Silicon, Windows x64 portable and Linux glibc x64 downloads. The application is free and MIT licensed; agent subscriptions are separate.

sources.title: Solenta changelog: release notes and new features
sources.finding: Shipped provider accounts, local models, MCP controls, schedules and SSH teleport are listed in release notes.

sources.title: Notifications and updates | Solenta docs
sources.finding: Desktop completion/decision notifications and a morning digest summarize unattended work.

sources.title: Build workflows | Solenta docs
sources.finding: Sequential phases can fan out across providers, retry interrupted work and use versioned repository templates.

sources.title: Codex sessions | Solenta docs
sources.finding: Interactive Codex has live steering and approvals; noninteractive workflow phases lack live steering. Native session ownership is protected.

sources.title: Import, eject and reclaim | Solenta docs
sources.finding: Import provider history, eject to a terminal and reclaim outside turns without duplicate messages.

sources.title: Project config files | Solenta docs
sources.finding: Shared solenta.json and local overrides define setup, quick actions and automations with command trust checks.

sources.title: Dev servers | Solenta docs
sources.finding: Managed servers use per-thread environment paths, optional readiness probes, retained command output and cleanup.

sources.title: Terminal and Browser panes | Solenta docs
sources.finding: Per-thread shell and loopback browser provide previews, screenshots and agent-visible diagnostics.

sources.title: Windows | Solenta documentation
sources.finding: The Windows doctor checks Git Bash, Node 22, long paths and WSL boundaries.

sources.title: Solenta README, usage ping
sources.locator: README.md lines 338-341 (Usage ping) and electron/telemetry.js lines 9-23, release v0.29.0 commit f46d238
sources.finding: Release builds send one anonymous usage ping a day (random install id, version, OS, architecture and agent CLIs used); setting DO_NOT_TRACK=1 or SOLENTA_TELEMETRY=0 turns it off, as the telemetry module checks.
